2. The properties of the petitioners were acquired in LA Case No. 41/64-65 and in other 22 LA Cases and there was dispute with regard to the award money in all the 23 cases which was ultimately settled by the 2nd Court of the then Subordinate Judge and Arbitrator, Dhaka allowing Arbitration Cases in all the 23 cases on various dates against the Government who filed appeals before the High Court Division which were subsequently dis- missed and the award passed by the Arbitrator on 18-3-1991 was affirmed. The petitioners then filed Money Execution Case No. 45 of 1995 including Money Execution Case No. 36 of 1995, 42 of 1995, 38 of 1995, 44 of 1995, 46 of 1995, 48 of 1995, 49 of 1995, 50 of 1995, 51 of 1995, 53 of 1995, 54 of 1995, 55 of 1995, 56 of 1995, 57 of 1995, 58 of 1995,41 of 1995,40 of 1995 and 39 of 1995. In Money Execution Case No. 45 of 1995 and in all other 22 Money Execution Cases the Arbitration amount was paid by excluding 6% of the amount in all the cases on the ground that 6% being "Utsha Kar" is deductable from the total Arbitration amount. The decree holder then filed applications in Money Execution Case NoA5 of 1995 including in all other execution cases praying for payment of 6% of the Arbitration amount on the ground that there was no reason for deducting 6% as "Utsha Kar". In the said execution cases, the judgment debtor government filed an application for rejecting the prayer of the decree holder for payment of 6% of the arbitration amount which was deducted by the judgment- debtor as "Utsha Kar" The Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka found that- 

 4. Being aggrieved thereby the decree-holder (petitioner) moved this Court and obtianed the present Rule. 

 5. A Y Masihuzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned District Judge committed a serious error of law in staying all the money execution cases by order dated 7-8-2006 and 28-9-2006 without assigning any reason whatsoever. The learned Advocate further submits that the awards in question were passed on 18-3-1991 and the money execution cases were filed on and from 19-8-1995 and the "Utsha Kar" was allegedly imposed by Finance Act of 1998 which came into operation on 1st July 1998 and this Act not having given any retrospective effect cannot have any effect on the decree passed before 1-7-1998 and this legal aspect was not noticed and considered by the learned District Judge. Mr Masih-uz- zaman further submits that the cultivators were deprived of their legitimate claim by deducting 6% as 'Utsha Kar' though no such utsha kar was to be deducted from the total arbitration amount granted by the Court of arbitrator and affirmed by the High Corut Division and the government had no authority to go beyond the decree and to deduct 6% of the arbitration amount as utsha kar. According to the learned Advocate, in any view, the government could not deduct 'utsha kar' at the rate of 6% on the toral arbitration amount and the learned District Judge committed an error of law in staying all further proceedings of the money execution cases without assigning any reason and overlooking that no provision of the Finance Act was made giving retrospective effect to the award money as passed on 18-3-1991 which was affirmed by the High Court Division in 1995 and the execution cases were filed in 1995. 

 7. I have perused the impugned order and considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for both the parties. Admittedly, the property belonging to the decree holder including 22 others was acquired in LA Case No. 41/64-65 including other LA cases and admittedly the final award money was settled by the 2nd Court of the then Subordinate Judge and the Court of arbitration on 18-3-1991 against which the judgment debtor being the government of Bangladesh preferred appeals before the High Court which were all dismissed some time in 1995. It is further admitted that Money Execution Case No. 45 of 1995 was filed on 13-8-1995 and other execution cases, as mentioned hereinabove, were also filed in 1995. It is not disputed that the amount of the Arbitration Award was paid to the decree holder of the present case including other decree holders deducting 6% therefrom as 'Utsha Kar'. As against deduction of 6% as "Utsha Kar', the decree holder in all the cases filed applications in Money Execution Case No. 45 of 1995 for directing the government for payment of 6% which was deducted as 'Utsha Kar' and the prayer was allowed directing the judgment-debtor government to deposit the balance amount on 15-11-2005 in the money execution cases. In the said money execution cases, the judgment-debtor filed an application for stay of all the money execution cases including Money Execution Case No. 45 of 1995 and the learned 2nd Court of the Joint District Judge, Dhaka rejected all the applications on the ground quoted there in above. Against the said order, the judgment- debtor Government of Bangladesh filed Civil Revision No.363 of 2006 before the District Judge, Dhaka which was out of time by 248 days. The learned District Judge by order dated 7-8-2006 condoned the said delay, admitted revision and stayed all further proceedings of money decree execution Case No.45 of 1995 till disposal of the Civil Revision. Subsequently, the judgment-debtor filed applications in Civil Revisional No.363 of 2006 for stay of all other money execution cases and the learned District Judge by the other impunged order dated 28-9-2006 stayed all further proceedings of all the money execution cases. It therefore, appears that the award was passed on 18-3-1991 and the alleged 'Utsha Kar' was introduced by the amendment of the Finance Act No.14 of 1998 which came into effect from 1st July, 1998. On a perusal of the provisions of the amended Finance Act, I do not find any provision giving any retrospective effect to any of the provisions of Finance Act No.14 of 1998 which came into force on and from 1st July, 1998. It therefore, appears that imposition of "Utsha Kar' in 1998 cannot have any effect in respect of the arbitration award which was allowed by the trial Court on 18-3-1991 and affirmed by the High Court Division in 1995 and the money execution cases were filed on 13-8-1995 and on various dates in 1995. This aspect was not at all noticed and considered by the learned District Judge while staying all further proceedings of Money Execution cases. The learned District Judge further stayed the operation of all further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 45 of 1995 without assigning any reason whatsoever. The learned District Judge further stayed all further proceedings of all other Money Execution Case Nos. 36 of 1995, 37 of 1995, 42 of 1995, 38 of 1995, 44 of 1995, 46 of 1995, 48 of 1995, 49 of 1995, 50 of 1995, 51 of 1995, 53 of 1995, 54 of 1995, 55 of 1995, 56 of 1995, 57 of 1995, 58 of 1995, 41 of 1995, 40 of 1995 and 38 of 1995 by one order dated 28-9-2006 on the basis of one application filed by the judgment-debtor in the said Civil Revision No. 363 of 2006 without at all assigning any reason for staying the aforesaid proceedings. The learned District Judge therefore committed serious error of law in staying the execution cases without assign ting any reason whatsoever. Mere filing of a revision case cannot be a ground for stay of all further proceedings of the decree unless there is cogent reason and sufficient cause for staying further proceedings of the decree. I am therefore, of the view that the impugned order suffers from illegality and irregularity which needs to be corrected by this Court in the exercise of its revisional jurisdiction. The pendency of the revision cases before the learned District Judge is no ground for staying further proceeding of the execution cases and the submission of the learned Assistant Attorney-General cannot therefore, be accepted.
